assets.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Make a SMALL, clearly visible camera-angle change to the supplied approved fictional man's portrait. Use this image as the ONLY identity and expression reference. Preserve his exact adult age and recognizable facial proportions.

VIEWPOINT:
A head-and-shoulders portrait, face directed about 20–25 degrees toward the viewer's right. This is a modest intermediate view between front and three-quarter, not a full 45-degree view. Move the camera sideways around the still subject at the same eye height; he keeps watching the same fixed person at his own eye height ahead of him and does not turn to follow the camera. Show a mild but real perspective difference: the far cheek, far eye and far nostril are slightly narrower, and the near ear becomes a little more visible. No head tilt or chin lift.

PRESERVE THE APPROVED STATE:
Keep the reference's settled, sustained gaze and very limited emotional feedback. Preserve its tight natural brow-to-upper-eyelid relationship, original eye opening and iris coverage by the upper lids, adapted only by perspective. Eyes stay directed level along the direction of his face, with no upward searching glance. Do not lift the brows, widen or squeeze the eyes, or add frown creases. Preserve a naturally wide resting mouth: lips softly closed, retaining original width and fullness, with neutral corners, no pursing, protrusion, downturned dissatisfaction or smile. He remains quietly observing; do not make him seem surprised, curious, questioning, worried, sleepy or awaiting reassurance.

IDENTITY:
Keep the same nose and its relation to the upper lip, same cheek fullness and gradual cheek-to-jaw taper. Preserve the whole continuous lower-lip/chin/jaw relationship and the reference's refined gently angular chin. Apply perspective rather than redesign: no separate chin pad, projecting nub, wider block chin, central cleft, compressed lower face or swollen cheek. Same short dark wavy hair, pale low-saturation gray-blue irises with dark rims, youthful ADULT skin and natural pores.

Keep the black shirt, textured dark jacket, subdued room, close framing and natural portrait-lens perspective. Preserve the broad directional side-light mood and readable sculptural shadows; do not evenly floodlight the newly visible cheek or add new eye highlights. One photorealistic color image, vertical 3:4, no text or collage.

Use case: identity-preserve.
Image 1 is the edit target. Image 2 is the approved SAME man's relaxed resting mouth reference only.

The previous small correction did not remove the gathered, narrow mouth. Make the mouth-corner release ACTUALLY VISIBLE, while keeping all other facial parts unchanged:
- Move the NEAR mouth corner (the leftmost end of the mouth as seen in the picture) a small but perceptible distance outward toward the cheek, approximately 5–7 percent of the current mouth width.
- Let the far mouth corner ease outward a smaller amount appropriate to its foreshortening.
- Reconnect these corners with a naturally extended, gently closed lip line. Preserve the central Cupid's bow and natural lip fullness. The relaxed opening is horizontal along the three-dimensional face, not stretched into a smile.
- The lips must no longer look bunched toward the center or puckered. Keep neutral corner height: neither raised nor pulled down. Retain a shallow natural fold below the lower lip and the current continuous chin/jaw contour.
The intended change is from a pursed closed mouth to an unhurried, comfortably resting closed mouth, with the specific lip identity in Image 2. Do not merely shave the center of the lower lip or brighten its shadow; correct the lateral corner positions and release the visible tension.

Preserve Image 1's exact eyes, brows, gaze direction, eyelid opening, pale gray-blue irises, nose, cheekbones, facial width and height, chin shape, adult age, hair, head position, small camera angle, directional lighting, clothing and background. Do not copy Image 2's front-facing perspective. No open mouth, smile, expression of surprise, pout or new face. One photorealistic color photograph, same vertical 3:4 composition.
